name: Pakistan
genZNote: 1947, same independence season as India, completely different constitutional path since. Two countries, one shared birthday week — August 14 and 15.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in South Asia, bordered by India (east), Afghanistan and Iran (west), and China (north, via the Karakoram range).
The Indus River and its tributaries form the country's agricultural backbone, flowing from the Himalayas/Karakoram to the Arabian Sea.
K2, the world's second-highest peak, sits in Pakistan's Karakoram Range.
Major cities: Islamabad (capital), Karachi (largest city, main port), Lahore, Faisalabad.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Urdu and English are the official languages; Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, and Balochi are widely spoken regional languages.
Culturally rooted in South Asian and Islamic traditions, sharing much of its Mughal-era architectural heritage with India.
Mohenjo-daro, an Indus Valley Civilization site, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Sindh province.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal parliamentary Islamic republic; the President is head of state, the Prime Minister heads the government.
Bicameral legislature: National Assembly (lower house) and Senate (upper house).
Formed in 1947 through the Partition of British India, becoming independent on 14 August 1947.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Member of the United Nations, SAARC, and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
A long-standing strategic partnership with China, including projects under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
sections.body: India and Pakistan share a complex bilateral relationship shaped by their shared 1947 Partition history, including unresolved disputes over Jammu & Kashmir. Diplomatic, trade, and people-to-people ties have varied significantly over different periods. This profile keeps to factual, neutral description rather than commentary on any specific dispute.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A textile- and agriculture-driven economy; cotton, textiles, and rice are among its major exports.
Karachi is the country's principal seaport and commercial hub.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: K2 and the Karakoram mountain range, Mohenjo-daro's Indus Valley ruins, and cricket as a major national sport.
Shared Partition history with India, marking both countries' independence in August 1947.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Pakistan is a federal parliamentary Islamic republic in South Asia, formed in 1947 through the Partition of British India.
keyFacts: Capital: Islamabad. Currency: Pakistani Rupee. Independence: 14 August 1947 (one day before India).
Home to K2, the world's second-highest mountain.
Mohenjo-daro (Indus Valley Civilization) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Pakistan.
commonConfusion: Pakistan's independence (14 August 1947) is one day BEFORE India's (15 August 1947) — a commonly mixed-up date pair.

highYieldFacts: K2 is located in Pakistan, not Nepal — a common mix-up with Everest (Nepal/China border).
Mohenjo-daro, an Indus Valley Civilization site, is in Pakistan (Sindh province), not India.
commonTraps: Assuming all Indus Valley Civilization sites are in India — Mohenjo-daro and Harappa are both in present-day Pakistan.
Mixing up Pakistan's and India's independence dates.
mustRemember: Pakistan formed via the 1947 Partition of British India; independence 14 August 1947.
